newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabia's annual food imports seen at $5 bln.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia's annual food imports seen at $5 bln.

text.p: Saudi Arabia imports about $5 billion worth of food every year, and the United States is seeking to expand its more than 15 percent share of that market, a U.S. official said in remarks published on Thursday.

The Saudi newspaper Arab News quoted Mohammad Haseebullah of the Jeddah-based U.S. Consulate's Agriculture Trade Office as saying the U.S. was promoting its products to expand its share of the food import market in the kingdom.

The newspaper quoted a U.S. consulate study as saying Saudi Arabia's food processing and packaging industry has more than $1 billion in investment commitments for the next three years. The industry is the kingdom's third largest manufacturing sector.
Haseebullah could not be reached for comment on Thursday, the start of the weekend in Saudi Arabia.

Saudi Arabia has the largest Gulf Arab market with a population of around 18 million. It is trying to diversify its oil-driven economy and has channelled revenues into projects turning its deserts into farms producing wheat and crops.

The kingdom's 1995-2000 development plan says its objectives for the food sector include diversifying output to contribute to food supply security. One way this will be done is by raising output of vegetables and fruits in greenhouses.
